observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a 4-thread overlock (serger) machine mounted on a flatbed industrial table, with thread cones, a foot pedal, and a red electronic motor control box showing a digit display.
Photo 2 shows a separate flatbed industrial straight-stitch (lockstitch) sewing machine head on a similar table stand, with a red box (possibly a servo motor cover) underneath.
The overlock machine's casing has small printed text and a logo, but it is too small/blurred to read a brand name clearly.
Table edges, paint and metal frame show scuff marks and handling wear in photos 0 and 1.
No serial number plate, power cable, or plug is clearly visible in any photo.
No photo shows the machines powered on, stitching, or producing a sample seam.

identity.kind: industrial lockstitch sewing machine and 4-thread overlock (serger) machine, sold as a set

claims.evidence: Photos 0 and 1 show scuff marks and wear on the table frame and machine housing, inconsistent with an unused item.
No photo shows a legible brand plate or label matching this name; text on the overlock casing is too small/blurred to confirm.
A red box resembling a servo/DC motor controller is visible under the table in photo 2, but no label or power-on shot confirms it is a DC motor.
Photo 0 and 1 show four thread cones feeding into the machine head, consistent with a 4-thread overlock design.

risks.risk: Motor and machine may not actually power on or stitch correctly
risks.proof: A short video of the machine running with thread, producing a stitched sample

risks.risk: Claimed 'brand new' status may be false; machine could be used/refurbished
risks.proof: Close-up photo of an unworn serial/brand plate and original packaging or receipt

risks.risk: Motor type (DC/servo vs clutch) affects value and efficiency
risks.proof: Clear photo of the motor label and control box markings

risks.risk: Missing accessories (power cable, plug, extra needles, bobbins) not shown
risks.proof: Photo of full accessory set included in the sale

risks.risk: Table/stand condition and stability not fully visible
risks.proof: Photo of all four table legs and the tabletop surface without obstruction

proof_requests: Video of each machine powered on and stitching a sample piece of fabric
Close-up of any brand/serial plate on both machine heads
Close-up of the motor control box label to confirm DC/servo type
Photo showing all accessories (cables, plug, pedal connections) included
Full, unobstructed photo of each table stand from base to top
response.reason: The two industrial machines (overlock and lockstitch) can be identified by type from the photos, but the 'brand new' and brand/motor-type claims are unverified or contradicted by visible wear, so they must be priced at worst case as used, unverified machines until further proof is given.
